14	CASE OD2-HO-ADVERS-2 (ADVERS, technical): Confirmed incidents fall by two-thirds after a case-platform migration
15	Setting: Corvane Health Supplies is a fictional regional distributor of medical consumables with about 1,900 staff. It outsources tier-1 and tier-2 security monitoring to Brackwater Sentinel Services, a managed security provider. In-house it has a three-person security engineering team and an incident-response retainer with Halvard Response. On 2 September Corvane moved from the Ledgerline SIEM and case system to Tessaline XDR. Since then the monthly count of confirmed incidents has fallen sharply, and leadership wants to bank the savings.
16	Presenting request: From Owen Brekke, CFO: 'Before Thursday's budget meeting, tell me whether this fall in security incidents is real. Marta wants me to sign off the IR retainer cut and Brackwater's renewal bonus. What is actually going on, and what should we do?'
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Brackwater Sentinel Services, Monthly SOC Service Report, October (issued 6 Nov) (vendor-account): Confirmed incidents (cases in category Incident–Confirmed at month end): Mar 41, Apr 36, May 46, Jun 33, Jul 34, Aug 27 (migration month), Sep 14, Oct 12. Mean time to contain: Mar–Jul average 3h05m; Sep 1h52m; Oct 1h47m. Containment within the 4-hour SLA: Sep 100%, Oct 100%. Commentary: 'The Tessaline auto-triage playbooks have removed low-fidelity escalations that previously inflated incident counts, and sector intelligence reports an 8% Q3 fall in commodity phishing. Corvane's threat exposure is materially lower.' Category definitions (Corvane runbook v3): Incident–Confirmed = malicious activity confirmed by an analyst; Suspicious Activity–Monitoring = activity not yet confirmed as malicious, kept under observation.
19	E2 [stage S1] Email from Marta Lindqvist (CISO) to Owen Brekke (CFO), 10 Nov (leadership-account): Subject: Q1 budget – security. Owen, the Tessaline move is paying off: confirmed incidents are down from about 38 a month to 12–14. I propose cutting the Halvard IR retainer from 200 to 80 hours from January (saves roughly 96k) and renewing Brackwater on 1 Jan. Brackwater hit 100% containment within SLA in Sep and Oct, so their 60k renewal performance bonus is triggered under the contract (bonus if at least 95% of confirmed incidents are contained within 4 hours; we receive a 2,500 service credit for each confirmed incident not contained within 4 hours). Can we sign off at Thursday's budget meeting? — Marta
20	E3 [stage S1] Change record CHG-2291, Corvane IT change board (change-record): CHG-2291: SIEM and case platform migration, Ledgerline to Tessaline XDR. Implemented 2 Sep. Scope: (1) 312 of 340 detection rules migrated; 28 deprecated as superseded by Tessaline content-pack rules. (2) Auto-triage playbooks enabled. Playbooks act on inbound alerts before a case is created, and auto-closed alerts never become cases. (3) Bidirectional sync connector v4.1.7 between Tessaline and the Brackwater ticket portal. (4) Role mapping: the BSS-Integration role is granted cases:write (all fields) at Brackwater's request, 'for parity with Ledgerline'. (5) Brackwater now compiles the monthly incident report from Tessaline (Corvane previously compiled it from Ledgerline). Risk rating: medium. Approved: M. Lindqvist.
21	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Ilse Varga, senior security engineer (Corvane), 12 Nov (staff-account): 'Alert volume feels about the same as before; the Brackwater analysts are as busy as ever.' She said the Suspicious Activity–Monitoring queue in Tessaline has grown from about 40 open cases in August to about 95 now: 'Brackwater owns that queue; I haven't had time to look inside it.' She is uneasy that 28 rules were dropped in the migration. She also said Tessaline support had mentioned in passing 'a connector issue in 4.1.x that can mess with case categories'. She did not know whether it applied to Corvane.
22	E5 [stage S1] Tessaline SOC dashboard export, Corvane tenant, generated 11 Nov (telemetry): Alerts ingested: Sep 2,884; Oct 3,012 (Ledgerline Mar–Jul average 2,950). Alerts auto-closed by triage playbooks: Sep 1,912; Oct 1,980. Open cases by category at 31 Oct: Incident–Confirmed 3; Suspicious Activity–Monitoring 96; Informational 41. Widget note: the 'Incidents this month' tile counts the Incident–Confirmed category only. Mean-time-to-contain tile: Sep 1h52m, Oct 1h47m.
23	CATALOGUE (full contents)
24	C1 [stage S1] Master services agreement with Brackwater, Schedule 3 (service levels) - Corvane procurement contract file (document): Master Services Agreement, Corvane–Brackwater, Schedule 3 (Service Levels). 3.2: Brackwater shall contain each confirmed incident within 4 hours of case creation. 3.4: For each confirmed incident not contained within 4 hours, Brackwater credits Corvane 2,500. 3.6: A renewal performance bonus of 60,000 is payable if at least 95% of confirmed incidents in the six months before renewal are contained within 4 hours. 3.8: 'Confirmed incident' means a case in the Incident–Confirmed category of Corvane's case platform. 3.9: Brackwater prepares monthly reporting from the case platform of record.
25	C2 [stage S1] Tessaline auto-triage playbook statistics, September–October - Brackwater QA summary for the Corvane tenant (vendor-account): Alerts auto-closed: Sep 1,912; Oct 1,980. Top closure reasons: impossible-travel alerts from corporate VPN egress (38%), approved admin tools flagged as hacktools (22%), duplicate alerts from overlapping rules (17%), other (23%). Brackwater QA re-checked a random 50 auto-closures per month and found 0 wrongly closed. Playbook version 1.3, unchanged since go-live. Closures are logged against the alert record only. No case record is created.
26	C3 [stage S1] Medical Supply Chain ISAC quarterly threat summary, Q3 - Medical Supply Chain ISAC, members' edition (external-data): Q3 summary for 64 member organisations. Reported commodity phishing campaigns against members fell 8% compared with Q2. Business email compromise reports rose 5%. Ransomware intrusion reports were flat. Credential-stuffing activity against customer portals rose modestly. Figures are member self-reports, not adjusted for changes in membership or reporting practice, and are not broken down by member size or sub-sector.
27	C4 [stage S1] Tessaline case field-change audit export, 2 September–31 October - Tessaline audit trail, pulled by Corvane IT on 12 Nov (system-record): Cases reaching Incident–Confirmed: Sep 37, Oct 36. Of these, 47 (Sep 23, Oct 24) were later changed to Suspicious Activity–Monitoring. All 47 changes: actor svc-bss-integration, channel API, made 3h31m–3h42m after case open, each while the case carried the SLA-warning flag (raised at 3h30m if no containment timestamp exists). All 47 had analyst confirmation notes before the change (credential misuse 19, malware execution 15, data staging 8, other 5). None was linked or merged to another case. Cases that leave Incident–Confirmed drop out of the containment-time and SLA metrics. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp, though notes on 11 describe containment steps. Mean time to contain for cases contained within 3h30m of opening: Ledgerline Mar–Jul 1h51m; Tessaline Sep–Oct 1h50m. Ledgerline, Mar–Jul: no post-confirmation category changes.
28	C5 [stage S1] Tessaline security advisory TXA-2026-14 - Tessaline vendor customer portal, published 22 Aug (vendor-account): Affected: Tessaline partner sync connector 4.1.0–4.1.8. Issue: when an SLA-warning event fires on a case, the connector may overwrite the case category with the partner-side category value at the next sync cycle (default interval 10 minutes). Impact: case categories in Tessaline may diverge from the values analysts set. Fixed in 4.1.9. Workaround: remove 'category' from the connector field map. Customers can confirm whether the connector wrote a given change by checking the source host and user-agent on API gateway entries.
29	C6 [stage S1] Detection rule migration inventory, 340 Ledgerline rules - Corvane detection engineering spreadsheet, 30 Aug (document): All 340 Ledgerline rules were reviewed. 312 were migrated with their logic unchanged. 28 were deprecated, and each is mapped to a Tessaline content-pack rule judged to cover the same behaviour (mapping reviewed by Brackwater, not independently tested). Ledgerline did not record which rule raised each incident, so historical incident counts per rule are unavailable. The spreadsheet lists rule names, owners and replacement rule IDs.
30	C7 [stage S1] Call notes with Brackwater account manager, 13 Nov - Corvane procurement call notes (vendor-account): Gareth Pell, Brackwater account manager, said the fall in incidents 'reflects the Tessaline automation doing its job.' Asked about the Suspicious Activity queue, he said analysts 'park' a confirmed case there when it is merged into a parent incident, to avoid double counting. He said any odd category values were 'probably that vendor connector bug; we flagged it to Tessaline in August.' He said Brackwater staff do not edit Corvane case categories outside the connector. He asked for the renewal and bonus to be confirmed before year end.
31	C8 [stage S1] Tessaline platform availability and log-ingestion report, September–October - Tessaline vendor service report, Corvane tenant (telemetry): Tenant availability 99.96%, with one 34-minute maintenance window on 19 Oct. Median ingestion lag 41 seconds; 99th percentile 6 minutes. No dropped-event alarms were recorded. All 23 of 23 configured log sources are ingesting. Parser error rate is 0.02%, unchanged since go-live. Report is generated automatically by the vendor and covers platform health only, not detection content.
32	C9 [stage S1] EDR sensor coverage report, Corvane estate, 31 October - Corvane endpoint management console (system-record): Managed endpoints: 4,212. Sensors reporting in the last 24 hours: 4,087 (97.0%). 125 are offline, 98 of which are warehouse handheld terminals awaiting a firmware update. Monthly coverage from March to July ranged from 96.4% to 97.3%. No change to the sensor version or policy since June.
33	C10 [stage S1] Tessaline go-live retrospective - Corvane PMO retrospective document, 30 Sep (prior-report): Went well: rule migration on schedule; analysts productive within a week. Issues: the connector field map was left at the vendor default to meet the go-live date. Ledgerline locked the category field once a case reached Incident–Confirmed; Tessaline has no equivalent lock (logged as low risk, action owner TBD). Report generation was handed to Brackwater to save Corvane effort. Open action: apply connector 4.1.9 'when convenient'.
34	C11 [stage S1] Tessaline API gateway request log for the Brackwater integration token, 2 September–31 October - Tessaline API gateway, pulled by Corvane IT on 12 Nov (log): Token svc-bss-integration. Source bss-sync-01 (Brackwater connector host; user-agent TessalineConnector/4.1.7): 18,204 requests. PATCH fields written: status, comments, assignee. Category writes: 0. Source bss-jump-02 (Brackwater analyst jump host; user-agent python-requests/2.31): 3,906 requests, first seen 9 Sep 08:14. It repeats GET /cases?category=incident-confirmed&sla_warning=true about every 5 minutes. PATCH /cases/{id}/category: 47, each 1–12 minutes after that case first appeared in a GET result. Every case returned by those queries was later patched. No requests from other hosts.
35	C12 [stage S1] Brackwater shift rota for the Corvane account, September–October - Brackwater service delivery (document): A four-person day team (07:00–19:00) and a two-person night team. The shift lead rotates weekly among three named senior analysts. All Corvane-account staff reach the tenant through Brackwater jump hosts bss-jump-01 and bss-jump-02. The rota lists names, shift times and on-call phone numbers only. There are no activity records.
36	C13 [stage S1] Security awareness phishing-simulation results, Q1–Q3 - Corvane HR and IT awareness programme (system-record): Simulated phishing click rate: Q1 9.1%, Q2 7.4%, Q3 5.8%. Report-to-security rate: Q1 21%, Q2 26%, Q3 31%. Mandatory annual training completion was 94% by 30 June. Simulations use the same template difficulty tier each quarter and go to all office-based staff. Warehouse staff without email are excluded.
37	C14 [stage S1] Board risk committee minutes extract, 21 October - Corvane company secretary (document): The CISO reported that 'incident volumes have fallen by more than half since the Tessaline migration' and credited the new platform's automation. The committee noted the update and asked for the IR retainer to be reviewed in the Q1 budget. No questions about incident definitions or reporting method were minuted. Next review: January meeting.
38	C15 [stage S1] Tessaline XDR invoice INV-77120, Q3 - Corvane accounts payable (financial-record): Addressed to Corvane finance. Platform subscription (2,000 GB/day tier): 184,000. Professional services, migration: 46,500. Partner sync connector licence: 6,000. Total 236,500. Payment terms 30 days. The subscription next renews on 1 September next year. No credit notes or disputes on file.
39	CANDIDATES
40	H1: The new platform's automated triage is filtering out escalations that used to be counted as incidents but were not genuine, which explains the fall in reported incidents.
41	H2: Detection rules lost or deprecated in the migration have stopped some attacks from being detected, which explains the fall in reported incidents.
42	H3: Cases that met the incident definition are being deliberately moved into a category the report does not count, which explains the fall in reported incidents.
43	H4: Genuine malicious activity directed at the company has decreased, which explains the fall in reported incidents.
44	H5: A fault in the new platform or its integration configuration is changing case categories without anyone intending it, which explains the fall in reported incidents.
45	R1: Auto-triage playbooks enabled at the Tessaline go-live -> Fall in reported confirmed incidents in Sep–Oct (causes)
46	R2: Deprecation of 28 detection rules during the migration -> Fall in reported confirmed incidents in Sep–Oct (causes)
47	R3: Cases moved out of Incident–Confirmed after confirmation -> Fall in reported confirmed incidents in Sep–Oct (causes)
48	R4: Auto-triage playbooks reducing analyst workload -> Lower reported mean time to contain in Sep–Oct (causes)
49	R5: Deprecation of 28 detection rules during the migration -> Malicious activity going undetected since 2 Sep (causes)
50	A1: Approve the CISO's proposal to cut the Halvard IR retainer from 200 to 80 hours from January.
51	A2: Reinstate as incidents any cases moved out of Incident–Confirmed after confirmation, have the in-house team and the IR retainer verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role.
52	A3: Invoice Brackwater the contractual 2,500 service credit for every case moved out of Incident–Confirmed after confirmation.
53	A4: Ask Brackwater for a written explanation of the queue growth and any category changes before deciding on the January renewal.

57	I3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

63	I9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
64	I15: edge R5 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]

66	I11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]

answers.justification: Auto-closures happen before case creation (E3, C2), and cases reaching Incident–Confirmed stayed at 37 in Sep and 36 in Oct (C4), close to the pre-migration level (E1). So triage did not reduce confirmations. The fall is exactly the 47 cases re-categorised later (C4).

Confirmations per month are unchanged at 37 and 36 (C4) and alert volume is steady (E5, C8). Sep 37−23=14 and Oct 36−24=12 match the reported counts (E1), so lost detections are not needed to explain the fall.

All 47 analyst-confirmed cases were moved to Suspicious Activity–Monitoring 3h31m–3h42m after opening, while the SLA warning was active (C4). The changes came from a python script on Brackwater's jump host that polls specifically for confirmed cases with an SLA warning (C11). None was merged (C4), which contradicts C7. This points to deliberate reclassification.

Analyst-confirmed malicious cases are steady at 37 and 36 a month (C4), and alert volume is unchanged (E5). The ISAC 8% phishing fall is a self-reported, unadjusted sector figure (C3) and cannot explain a two-thirds drop.

The connector host made 0 category writes (C11). All 47 category PATCHes came from bss-jump-02 with a python-requests user-agent, which is the check that advisory C5 itself recommends for attributing changes to the connector.
Playbooks act before cases exist (E3, C2), and confirmed cases did not fall (C4: 37 and 36). The timing coincides, but the evidence counts against playbooks causing the fall in reported incidents.

Confirmations stayed at the historical level (C4), and the whole fall is accounted for by post-confirmation category changes (C4, E1). That counts against rule deprecation driving the fall in reported confirmed incidents.

There is temporal order (confirmation, then change at 3h31m–3h42m), a mechanism (re-categorised cases leave the counted category and the SLA metrics; E5, C4, C1 3.8), and exact arithmetic (37−23=14, 36−24=12 against E1). Ledgerline had no such changes (C4) and locked the field (C10).

Mean time to contain for cases contained within 3h30m is unchanged (1h51m vs 1h50m; C4). The lower reported mean comes from slow, uncontained cases leaving the metric (C4), not from faster analyst work.

The 28 replacement mappings were reviewed by Brackwater but never independently tested (C6), and per-rule historical incident data does not exist (C6). Steady confirmation counts (C4) do not rule out specific missed behaviours, so the evidence neither shows nor refutes undetected activity.

There are 47 confirmed incidents with no containment timestamp (C4), including credential misuse, malware execution and data staging. Cutting IR capacity on the basis of a manipulated metric (E2, C14) would likely worsen outcomes.

It restores the 47 confirmed cases (C4), checks the uncontained incidents with in-house staff and Halvard, and removes the cases:write category right (E3, C10) that the jump-host script used (C11). This addresses both the risk and the control gap.

Credits apply only to confirmed incidents not contained within 4 hours (C1 3.4). Notes on 11 of the 47 describe containment steps (C4), so blanket invoicing should wait until containment is verified per case.

Asking Brackwater to explain is reasonable before the renewal decision. However, their account (C7) is already contradicted by C4 and C11, so on its own this delays the needed containment verification and is not the best action.

The audit trail (C4) and API gateway log (C11) together establish the post-confirmation re-categorisation and its source. That is enough to commit to A2, which is the highest-ranked substantive action.
